title: You look clean on the outside…
paragraphs:
You look clean on the outside…
but something inside you is rotting.
And you know it.

You can lift your hands in worship
and still hide habits you hope nobody ever sees.

You can quote Scripture
and still be losing battles in secret.
So here’s the question that refuses to leave:
What is actually growing in you?

Not what you post.
Not what you perform.
Not what people applaud.
But what is growing… when no one is watching?
Because fruit doesn’t lie.
A tree can’t fake what it produces.

And your life—yes, yours—
is producing something right now.

Maybe it’s anger you can’t control.
Maybe it’s lust you keep feeding in the dark.
Maybe it’s pride dressed up as confidence.
Maybe it’s jealousy you justify as “motivation.”
Maybe it’s bitterness you rehearse every night.

You call it stress.
You call it weakness.
You call it “I’m just human.”
But Scripture calls it something else.
The flesh.

And the flesh doesn’t just whisper.
It grows.

Slow.
Quiet.
Hidden.
Until one day… it shows.
Paul doesn’t sugarcoat it.
“The works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality, idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, fits of anger, rivalries, dissensions, divisions, envy…” (Galatians 5:19–21)
That’s not a random list.
That’s a mirror.
And if you’re honest… you’ve seen yourself there.
This is where shame creeps in.
You start thinking:

“I should be better by now.”
“God must be tired of me.”
“I’m too inconsistent.”
“I’m too far gone.”
But listen carefully.

Shame will push you away from God.
Grace will pull you toward Him.
And this is where everything shifts.
Because Paul doesn’t stop with the flesh.
He pivots.
Hard.
“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control…” (Galatians 5:22–23)
Did you catch that?

Not fruits.
Not options.
Not personality traits.
Fruit.

One source.
One life.
One Spirit producing a transformed character.
This is not behavior modification.
This is transformation from the inside out.

Some scholars interpret this passage as a contrast not just between good and bad behavior, but between two sources of life—living by the flesh versus living by the Spirit. One produces death over time. The other produces life that looks like Jesus.
And here’s the truth that will set you free:
You cannot produce this fruit by trying harder.

You can’t grind your way into love.
You can’t discipline your way into peace.
You can’t force yourself into holiness.

Because the flesh can imitate…
but it cannot transform.
So what do you do?
You go back to the root.
Jesus said:
“Abide in Me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit by itself… neither can you, unless you abide in Me.” (John 15:4)
Read that again.

You don’t manufacture fruit.
You remain connected.
This is where the Gospel comes alive.

You are not saved because you fixed your behavior.
You are saved because Jesus took your sin.

Every hidden struggle.
Every secret failure.
Every moment of compromise.
He carried it to the cross.
“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)

Not when you were clean.
Not when you were consistent.
While you were still a mess.
That means your shame is not your final story.
Your failure is not your identity.
Your secret sin is not stronger than the blood of Jesus.
But grace is not permission to stay the same.
Grace is power to become new.
“Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.” (Galatians 5:24)
That word—crucified—is not gentle.
It’s decisive.
It means you stop making peace with the thing that’s killing you.
You stop feeding what Jesus died to free you from.

You don’t excuse it.
You don’t rename it.
You surrender it.
And then…
You walk.
“If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit.” (Galatians 5:25)
Step by step.
Day by day.
Moment by moment.
Not perfection.
But direction.
And slowly… something changes.

You respond differently.
You think differently.
You desire differently.
Not because you forced it—
But because the Spirit is producing something new in you.

Love where there used to be hate.
Peace where there used to be chaos.
Self-control where there used to be addiction.
This is not hype.
This is holiness.
So let me ask you again.
What is growing in you?
Because whatever you are feeding… will eventually show.
But here’s the hope:
It’s not too late to change the source.
Right now.

Not tomorrow.
Not when you “feel ready.”
Now.
Come back to Jesus.

Not with excuses.
Not with performance.
With honesty.
With surrender.
With repentance.
“Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.” (Psalm 51:10)
That prayer still works.
That mercy is still available.
That grace is still flowing.

You are not too dirty.
You are not too broken.
You are not too far gone.
Jesus doesn’t just forgive your sin.
He transforms your life.
So today—
Drop the mask.
Kill the secret.
Run to Christ.
Let the Spirit grow something real in you.
Not noise.
Not image.
Fruit.
If this hit your heart…
